comment: Single source of truth for the two Slack progress literals duplicated across languages: the block_id prefix every block of a progress card carries, and the one every block of a progress milestone carries (ADR-0130). The Python worker owns them as PROGRESS_CARD_BLOCK_ID_PREFIX and PROGRESS_MILESTONE_BLOCK_ID_PREFIX in apps/worker/src/curie_worker/blocks.py, where progress_card and progress_milestone stamp them; the Rust CLI owns independent copies of the same names in cli/src/chat.rs, whose presence on a block of a captured Slack call body is how the stub tells a progress post or edit from the turn's answer. The two lanes cannot share code across Python/Rust, so the literals are frozen here: changing one language without changing this file fails that language's test. Read by apps/worker/tests/test_blocks_progress.py's test_progress_block_ids_match_the_frozen_vector and by the test module in cli/src/chat.rs. The Python lane checks that its constants equal these values AND that every block either builder renders carries its own prefix and never the other one, so a new block added without a block_id is caught with no test edit; the Rust lane checks its constants equal these values. Lose that and the CLI stub reads a progress card as the answer: `local message`, `cluster message` and local eval report a status line as the turn's reply. Both lanes reject unknown top-level keys (ProgressBlockVector's deny_unknown_fields in Rust, _EXPECTED_PROGRESS_VECTOR_KEYS in Python), so adding a key here without teaching both lanes fails both: a key one lane cannot see would otherwise pass vacuously.
